output.summary: KEP-3726 rephrases the Service port appProtocol field description and declares standard kubernetes.io-prefixed protocol names (e.g. kubernetes.io/h2c) for common protocols that are not IANA service names. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: The appProtocol field only pointed to IANA service names or domain-prefixed names, so implementations gave the same value different meanings (HTTP2 means TLS in GKE but h2c in Istio). The proposal fixes this by defining well-known kubernetes.io-prefixed names for common protocols. The sources state the goals of building consensus and helping implementations interoperate, but do not give further reasons for the chosen approach.

alternatives.option: Keep IANA service names or domain-prefixed names only
alternatives.why_not: The motivation says this loose definition led implementations to do different things for common protocols, such as HTTP2 in GKE versus Istio.

alternatives.option: Support multiple appProtocol values for the same port
alternatives.why_not: It is listed as a non-goal, suggested as follow-up work.
Validation and monitoring of appProtocol implementations are explicit non-goals of this KEP.

evidence.quote: This loose definition has led us to; 1. Have instances where implementations do different things for common protocols.
This KEP suggests a different description for the `AppProtocol` field and proposes to declare standard Kubernetes protocol names for common protocols that are not IANA service names.
Those common protocols will be well defined strings prefixed with ‘kubernetes.io’. `kubernetes.io/h2c` as an example.
Support multiple AppProtocols values for the same port to improve interoperability (suggested as a followup work though)
